items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: Ory sent for me, you know what I played.

ctx.x: Oh, I heard of him, too.

Yeah. See? Did he pick the bass? He was picking, picking, picking, wasn't slapping, just picking. Picking it. Oh, yes. See? So, so, they can't, they can't give those, those guys credit. But when I come, when I went around New York, when I left Los Angeles, even in L.A., in 22, there wasn't no string bass out here but me and Montuti. See, nobody didn't pay no attention to Montuti. Didn't start to pay attention to Montuti until I come out here with the Ory band. After I went, Ory went with the black and tan band,…

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: He had Billy Butler, a guy called Bonner, myself, Mutt. Bud Scott, and he had a very good band.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. Don, did you have some lunch? No, I'm all right. Would you like something? Anything you, would you like a drink? Or- Get some stuff from downstairs. Do you want anything? No, not right now. All right. Thanks. What's that, what? That's the recorder. What happened? If that's the recorder, they come with noise. You see me making noise noise? Well, sure. The machine's gone, broke down. That's what's happened. It broke? The machine broke? No. No. Cutting contest. That's what I call a cutting contest. No,…

Mm-hmm. That's a pretty good band. Mm-hmm. There they are in the band, they hired me back that Friday. Uh-huh. That's a pretty good band. There they are in the band, they hired me back that Friday.
